policies.summary: A commission site permit for a large energy infrastructure facility is the only site approval needed and supersedes and preempts all regional, county, local and special purpose government zoning, building and land use rules for the facility.

A large electric power generating plant may not be sited where its developed portion uses more than 0.5 acres of prime farmland per MW unless there is no feasible and prudent alternative; the rule does not apply inside or near cities.

The Public Utilities Commission issues site permits for solar and other generating plants of 50 MW or more, wind of 5 MW or more and storage of 10 MW or more; smaller projects need no commission permit but must still get any local, state or federal approval that applies and meet state environmental review rules. Applicants for solar and generating plants under 80 MW, wind under 25 MW and any storage system may instead seek local approval, unless a local unit of government asks the commission to take the case within 60 days.

restrictions.description: Regional energy grid infrastructure, high-voltage utility demand, and public safety concerns common to both data centers and battery energy storage systems; staff reported needing the full extended year to finish the data center ordinance after spending the prior year on the energy-storage-system framework. Active (extended) as of 2026-09-23. The County Board voted unanimously on August 18, 2026 to extend the moratorium on data centers (originally adopted August 2025) for a second consecutive year, through August 19, 2027, finding that allowing it to lapse would threaten public safety and orderly development because current regulations are inadequate. Planning and Zoning Administrator Trevor Bordelon said his office would need the full additional year to develop the data-center ordinance, having spent the prior year on a parallel energy-storage-system framework intended to serve as a foundation for high-load utility planning generally. Legal basis: Temporary interim zoning ordinance on data centers, adopted by the Freeborn County Board of Commissioners in August 2025 (alongside a parallel moratorium on energy storage systems, due to overlapping grid-infrastructure concerns); extended for a second year (through Aug. 19, 2027) by unanimous County Board resolution on August 18, 2026, under Minnesota Statutes Chapter 394.
